There you will find an active community of JKI software users, as well as JKI team members.\0A\0AHow to use:\0A\0AFind the JKI State Machine in the palettes\0A1) Functions >> JKI Toolkits >> JKI State Machine\0A\0AUse QuickDrop to place a JKI State Machine on the block diagram\0A1)  Press Control+Space then type "JKI"\0A2) choose the "JKI State Machine" option that appears\0A\0ALaunch the JKI State Machine Explorer by either\0D\0AA) Right-click on a State String, Case Structure, or Event Structure to launch JKI SM Editor\0D\0AB) Press Control+Space then Control+J when you're on the block diagram of a VI containing a JKI SM\0A\0D\0D\0AUsing the Right-click menu on the JKI SM Parts for increased productivity:\0D\0A- Select an item in the tree to make that frame visible\0D\0A- Click back and forward to navigate the history\0D\0A- Drag and drop frames to reorganize the order\0D\0A- Right-click on items in the tree-view to rename, duplicate, delete, etc.\0D\0A- Right-click on a state string and choose Goto State Frame to jump to that frame of the JKI SM.\0A- Right click on a state string or frame and choose Find Callers to find all callers of a state\0A- Right-click on a bundle or unbundle by name and choose Find Data Accessors to find all accessors of the data.\0D\0A\0D\0ASpecial thanks to Jim Carmody for open sourcing his CaseSelect tool as a launching off point for the JKI SM Editor."
